user.title: Connect to the IHC controller
user.description:
Enter the address of the controller and a user that may sign in to it. The integration reads the project from the controller and creates a device for every product it finds.

A new controller starts in read-only mode: everything is shown, nothing is switched. Turn that off in the options when you are ready.

data_description.url: For example http://192.168.1.3. Use https:// if the controller is set up for it.
data_description.username: An IHC user. A user with read access is enough to look, and control needs a user that may operate the installation.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in to the IHC controller again
reauth_confirm.description: The controller at {url} no longer accepts the saved login.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the controller at that address.
error.invalid_auth: The controller refused that username and password.

abort.already_configured: This controller is already set up.

data_description.read_only: While this is on, the integration never sends a command to the installation. Entities still show what the house is doing, and any attempt to switch something says so.
data_description.expose_buttons: Create an event entity for every key on every wall switch, so automations can trigger on a press. The keys keep doing what the installation already uses them for.

read_only.message: This IHC controller is set up read-only. Turn off read-only mode in the integration options to control the installation from Home Assistant.
